ucc-of-fredericksburg.assessment: The United Church of Christ of Fredericksburg belongs to the most progressive mainline denomination in American Protestantism. The UCC was the first denomination to ordain an openly gay minister (1972) and the first to affirm same-sex marriage (2005). The denomination's 'God is still speaking' campaign and social justice emphasis define its institutional identity. While individual UCC congregations can theoretically be more conservative, the denominational DNA is thoroughly progressive. Rev. Darryl Moch leads. Not recommended for anyone committed to biblical authority and historic orthodoxy.

score_notes.christology: UCC denomination does not require trinitarian affirmation at congregational level; wide theological diversity.
score_notes.scripture: UCC does not affirm inerrancy; Scripture is 'a witness' not final authority in UCC theology.
score_notes.gender: UCC is the most progressive mainline denomination — first to ordain openly gay clergy (1972), first to affirm same-sex marriage (2005). Fully egalitarian.
score_notes.leadership: UCC congregational polity — local governance, but denominational identity is thoroughly progressive.
score_notes.soteriology: UCC theology ranges from universalist to loosely evangelical at the congregational level.
score_notes.cultural: Homepage describes itself as 'a church of extravagant welcome' that 'welcomes and accepts everyone as they are' and aims to 'encourage tolerance, promote social justice' — affirming/progressive UCC posture confirmed on landing page.
score_notes.preaching: Not stated on available sources — verify in person.
score_notes.mission: Stated mission language is 'together, we grow a just and peaceful world' — social-justice framing replaces Great-Commission language; aligns with UCC national identity.
score_notes.denominational: UCC is the most theologically liberal mainline denomination in America.

ucc-of-fredericksburg.gender_detail: UCC fully egalitarian at every level; LGBTQ+ clergy affirmed since 1972
